primitives.name: Skellam Score Difference
primitives.verbatim_quote: 2017): Skellam2(μ, σ2) with μ = θ1-θ2, σ2 = θ1+θ2, so covariates enter the mean linearly: μ_jk = α + β_j + γ_k (team j home vs team k; β_j = home ability, γ_k = away ability; baseline team Bergischer HC; team-specific home advantage = β_j - γ_j).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ': 'mean difference in goals, dimensionless', 'σ²': 'variance of difference, dimensionless', 'θ₁': 'home team expected goals, dimensionless', 'θ₂': 'away team expected goals, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Score differences follow Skellam distribution; underdispersed Poisson marginals imply valid Skellam use.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When score variance exceeds mean, Skellam fails; requires alternative modeling.

layer2.mapping: Skellam difference models score disparity as stochastic process; GSI infers posterior over team abilities via MLE.
layer2.telemetry: Match outcome probability, score difference PMF

primitives.name: Zero-Inflated Skellam
primitives.verbatim_quote: Extensions: (a) **zero-inflated Skellam** with extra parameter p (fit by EM; p optionally logistic in covariates z_i'γ); (b) **discretized normal** P_N(z) = Φ(z+0.5)-Φ(z-0.5); (c) **discretized Laplace** P_L(z) = F(z+0.5)-F(z-0.5).
primitives.latex: P_Z(z) = p + (1-p)P(z) \text{ if } z=0; (1-p)P(z) \text{ if } z\neq 0
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p': 'probability of zero inflation, dimensionless', 'P(z)': 'Skellam PMF, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Excess zeros in score differences due to draws or pushes; modeled via mixture with point mass at zero.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observed zeros exceed theoretical Skellam expectation, zero-inflation improves fit.

layer2.mapping: ZI-Skellam extends base Skellam to handle draw prevalence; GSI treats p as push probability in betting context.

primitives.name: Bivariate Half Score Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Bivariate.** First-half and second-half score differences (Y1, Y2) each marginally Skellam2, joined by a copula (Frank — allows negative/positive dependence — or Gumbel — tail dependence), with the discrete joint PMF via copula CDF differencing.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Y₁': 'first-half score difference, integer', 'Y₂': 'second-half score difference, integer', 'C': 'copula function, dimensionless', 'F, G': 'marginal CDFs, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Half-time differences are dependent; joint distribution modeled via copula linking marginal Skellams.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When half-time dependencies are ignored, conditional outcome forecasts become inaccurate.

layer2.mapping: Copula-based bivariate model encodes halftime dynamics; GSE computes conditional win/cover probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Halftime-conditional win probability, over/under coverage risk

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that handball scoring exhibits underdispersion, violating standard Poisson assumptions. The Skellam distribution, which models the difference of two independent Poisson variables, becomes applicable because even underdispersed marginals produce valid Skellam differences. This justifies modeling score differences rather than raw scores. The zero-inflated extension addresses frequent ties or pushes in handball. For bivariate modeling, the Frank or Gumbel copulas allow flexible dependence structures between first and second half differences, enabling accurate halftime-conditioned predictions. These primitives form a coherent framework for probabilistic forecasting and live betting surface generation.
